questions.0.explain.t: Every request is authenticated, authorized and evaluated, whether inside or outside the network.

questions.0.options.0.t: Never trust, always verify: no network or origin is trusted by default

questions.0.q.t: What is the core principle of Zero Trust?

questions.1.explain.t: The perimeter no longer exists as a single barrier; identity and device posture decide.

questions.1.options.0.t: The access decision moves from the network to identity and context

questions.1.q.t: What changes from the perimeter model to Zero Trust?

questions.2.explain.t: Full access over the VPN is the opposite: one stolen credential opens everything.

questions.2.options.0.t: Per-request access with MFA and least privilege

questions.2.options.1.t: VPN with full access to the internal network
